statement: genes-ts supports controlled Haxe-to-TypeScript and classic ESM JavaScript profiles. This evidence inventory maps bounded Genes product claims and one six-test official Haxe smoke subset to exact gates; it is not a blanket certification of arbitrary Haxe or npm programs and does not claim the complete applicable official Haxe suite.

statusSemantics.blocking: The named gate is required by core CI/release.
statusSemantics.nonblockingNightly: The named pressure test reports evidence without blocking core changes.
statusSemantics.liveResultLocation: GitHub Actions; this deterministic file is not a cached run log.

classes.label: Compile inventory
classes.meaning: Sources and declared profiles compile under their owned gates; compilation alone is not semantic or public-type proof.

classes.label: Strict public typing
classes.meaning: Positive consumers compile and selected invalid consumers are rejected without broad public any/unknown/index signatures.

classes.label: Semantic differential
classes.meaning: Named runtime traces agree across the explicitly listed oracles; the result applies only to those contracts.

classes.label: Snapshot stability
classes.meaning: Generated source shape is deterministic relative to reviewed snapshots; snapshots do not establish semantics by themselves.

classes.label: Runtime smoke and E2E
classes.meaning: Named application journeys execute in selected profiles; smoke success is not general semantic parity.

classes.label: Toolchain compatibility
classes.meaning: Generated output and programmatic compiler APIs are checked on separately owned, pinned lanes.

classes.label: Package-shape interoperability
classes.meaning: Named ESM, subpath, conditional-export, CommonJS, and declaration-ingestion fixtures work under their tested resolution modes.

classes.label: Downstream pressure tests
classes.meaning: Pinned WIP consumers provide nonblocking integration evidence; failures are not compiler defects until reduced to a generic compiler fixture.

productSurfaces.label: Classic JavaScript generation and runtime
productSurfaces.owner: Classic emitter and shared Haxe runtime owners
productSurfaces.claim: Ordinary Haxe programs in the reviewed corpus compile to split ESM JavaScript and preserve the exercised Haxe runtime behavior.
productSurfaces.claimCeiling: The checked compiler and example corpora; not arbitrary Haxe ecosystem compatibility.
productSurfaces.lastCleanProof: The current required main/release gates; run results live in GitHub Actions rather than this deterministic manifest.
residualRisks: The complete applicable official Haxe inventory is registration evidence only; representative runtime expansion remains separate from the six-test smoke.

productSurfaces.label: Typed TypeScript generation and runtime
productSurfaces.owner: TypeScript emitter and TypeScript semantic plans
productSurfaces.claim: The reviewed Haxe corpus emits strict, executable TypeScript with the asserted public and runtime semantics.
productSurfaces.claimCeiling: The checked TypeScript 5/6/7 contracts and fixtures; not all possible Haxe or TypeScript programs.
productSurfaces.lastCleanProof: The current required main/release gates; run results live in GitHub Actions rather than this deterministic manifest.
residualRisks: Generated-source readability still requires reviewed shape assertions in addition to strict type checking.

productSurfaces.label: Declarations and package contracts
productSurfaces.owner: Declaration reachability, type emitters, and package/import plans
productSurfaces.claim: Reviewed classic declarations and package-shaped imports retain precise, consumable public contracts.
productSurfaces.claimCeiling: The checked declaration consumers and package fixtures; runtime success alone cannot advance this claim.
productSurfaces.lastCleanProof: The current required main/release gates; run results live in GitHub Actions rather than this deterministic manifest.
residualRisks: Third-party package contracts outside the curated fixtures remain independent evidence.

productSurfaces.label: React, HXX, JSX, and TSX compiler behavior
productSurfaces.owner: HXX parser, JSX semantic plan, React helpers, and source emitters
productSurfaces.claim: Reviewed HXX and React source shapes compile, type-check, map, and execute consistently across their declared source/createElement profiles.
productSurfaces.claimCeiling: Compiler-facing React/HXX behavior; it does not by itself prove a real browser application.
productSurfaces.lastCleanProof: The current required main/release gates; run results live in GitHub Actions rather than this deterministic manifest.
residualRisks: Framework-version and browser behavior require the separate browser/application scorecard.

productSurfaces.label: Browser and framework runtime behavior
productSurfaces.owner: Maintained application QA and Playwright observers
productSurfaces.claim: The maintained Todo application runs its distinctive browser workflow in both generated profiles.
productSurfaces.claimCeiling: The maintained browser scenarios and pinned framework versions; compiler-only React fixtures cannot advance this claim.
productSurfaces.lastCleanProof: The current required main/release gates; run results live in GitHub Actions rather than this deterministic manifest.
residualRisks: A browser scenario protects only the user-visible workflow it actually executes.

productSurfaces.label: Host tooling and publication helpers
productSurfaces.claim: The reviewed host lifecycle and publication primitives work through their protocol, runtime, clean-consumer, and transaction tests.
productSurfaces.claimCeiling: Framework-neutral primitives only; no framework-specific watcher or deployment policy is implied.
productSurfaces.lastCleanProof: The host-tooling gate owns live proof in required CI; no compatibility bucket or cached green result is asserted here.
residualRisks: Framework integrations must provide their own real host/runtime evidence.

productSurfaces.label: TypeScript-to-Haxe migration tooling
productSurfaces.claim: The documented ts2hx subset translates its checked fixtures transactionally and passes its semantic/runtime comparisons.
productSurfaces.claimCeiling: The proven migration subset only; it is not arbitrary TypeScript support and does not prove Haxe-to-Genes conformance.
productSurfaces.lastCleanProof: The current required main/release gates; run results live in GitHub Actions rather than this deterministic manifest.
residualRisks: Unsupported TypeScript syntax and project configurations remain explicit migration boundaries.

productSurfaces.label: Installation, release, adoption, and downstream contracts
productSurfaces.owner: Package, release, security, and curated downstream owners
productSurfaces.claim: The reviewed artifacts install cleanly, preserve their declared package shape, and are checked against pinned downstream contracts without laundering those results into compiler conformance.
productSurfaces.claimCeiling: Pinned package and downstream contracts; nonblocking downstream observations cannot promote a core compiler claim.
productSurfaces.lastCleanProof: Blocking package/release proof lives in required Actions. Curated downstream proof is nonblocking-nightly and exists only in its latest run artifact; this manifest does not cache a green result.
residualRisks: Unpinned consumers and unsupported ecosystems remain outside the release claim.

productSurfaces.label: Maintained example portfolio
productSurfaces.claim: Every immediate maintained example is classified and executes no more evidence than its declared tier and profile contract.
productSurfaces.claimCeiling: Examples are evidence assets, not a substitute for the product surface that owns the behavior.
productSurfaces.lastCleanProof: The current required main/release gates; run results live in GitHub Actions rather than this deterministic manifest.
residualRisks: A compile-only future example must not be advertised as runtime or migration proof.

buckets.label: Classic JavaScript and TypeScript output inventory
buckets.scope: Classic Genes runtime tests, generated TypeScript snapshot profiles, and every checked-in example in both first-class output profiles.

metrics.label: Examples with TS and classic profiles

buckets.proves: The enumerated compiler fixtures and examples compile under their owned TS/classic profiles.
buckets.doesNotProve: Compilation does not prove closed public types, runtime equivalence, arbitrary ecosystem compatibility, or an official upstream Haxe-suite result.

buckets.label: Closed exported surfaces and strict declaration consumers
buckets.scope: Generated TS exports, ordinary interfaces, explicit foreign boundaries, classic declarations, and strict external consumers.
buckets.proves: Every manifest-owned type module in the named generated profiles is either semantically audited or given an exact stale-detecting classification; strict consumers reject the named unsafe programs, and one opt-in library graph has matched retained TS/classic runtime and declaration surfaces.
buckets.doesNotProve: An exact runtime, fixture, or known-gap classification does not itself prove that foreign boundary sound; the audit also cannot infer soundness for untested raw metadata or every third-party declaration package.

buckets.label: Same-source compiler and ts2hx semantic differentials
buckets.scope: Haxe-to-TS/classic evaluation traces plus ts2hx strict-js control-flow, module-order, and typed package-binding contracts across original TypeScript, classic Genes, and genes-ts, with a separate standard-Haxe capability boundary.

metrics.label: ts2hx supported and fail-closed semantic input modules

buckets.proves: Named original-TypeScript, classic Genes, and genes-ts traces preserve the supported synchronous typed return/break/continue path through nested finalizers and the closed typed package boundary. Package evidence covers default, named, alias, static namespace, duplicate, primitive constant/function, Void, request order, once-only initialization, unused verbatim retention, and TS 5/6/7 generated output. Thirteen canonical ts2hx boundaries still fail closed, including broader package declarations, excluded async completion, standard-Haxe request rejection, and same-server isolation of the private Genes request capability.
buckets.doesNotProve: The synchronous contract does not cover excluded async/generator/constructor/anonymous/labeled/generic/weak-carrier/unsupported-loop forms. Package evidence does not cover mutable exports, overloads, object or union types, namespace identity/computed access, transform-synthesized binding uses, attributes, or arbitrary package export conditions. The standard-Haxe request rejection is a capability test rather than a fourth runtime-parity oracle; the curated traces are neither a language-wide proof nor a portability promise for other Haxe targets.

buckets.label: Reviewed genes-ts and ts2hx snapshots
buckets.scope: Generated TypeScript/TSX and supported ts2hx Haxe source shapes.
buckets.proves: The exact generated forms remain stable unless reviewers intentionally update their baselines.
buckets.doesNotProve: A stable snapshot can preserve a bug; semantic and typing gates remain authoritative.

buckets.label: Same-source examples and todoapp browser E2E
buckets.scope: The minimal example and fullstack todoapp compile from one Haxe source tree through TS and classic ESM profiles.

metrics.label: Todoapp browser journeys run in each profile

buckets.proves: Both outputs build and execute the same selected application workflows, including status filtering, validation, CRUD, navigation, and deep links.
buckets.doesNotProve: Two green examples do not imply whole-ecosystem or framework-independent parity.

buckets.label: Pinned official Haxe 4.3.7 active registration inventory
buckets.scope: The exact upstream unit entry point is typed under each Genes JavaScript profile to record active conditional, standard-library specification, and issue-regression registrations.

metrics.label: Reviewed active official Haxe test registrations per profile

buckets.proves: The pinned Haxe entry point registers the reviewed 1,373 test identities in each exact profile, and injected profile or cached-source drift stays red.
buckets.doesNotProve: Registration inventory does not compile these tests with Genes, target-check generated files, run the tests, or report runtime compatibility.

buckets.label: Pinned official Haxe 4.3.7 dual-profile smoke
buckets.scope: Six exact official Haxe tests from shared language, unitstd, and issue families compile through a packaged Genes artifact in classic and TypeScript profiles, pass each target checker, and execute 45 assertions per profile under Node.

metrics.label: Reviewed active official Haxe test identities

buckets.proves: The published six-test official Haxe 4.3.7 smoke subset passes after target checking and runtime execution in each Genes profile, and the harness fails closed for generation, target, module-load, assertion, runtime, timeout, and missing-test failures.
buckets.doesNotProve: Six tests do not establish the complete active official tests/unit contract, capability coverage, Haxe preview compatibility, or any Genes-native declaration, HXX, package, source-map, transaction, or application claim outside the smoke.

buckets.label: Pinned generated-output and compiler-API lanes
buckets.scope: Stable/current Node, stable/preview Haxe, TS5/TS6/TS7 generated output, the TS6 program API, and dts2hx's TS5.9 converter API.

metrics.label: Pinned Node lanes, runtime floors, and supported range

buckets.proves: Generated code and API consumers are checked against their explicitly different compatibility contracts, and ts2hx request evidence records the exact pinned TypeScript engine and configured transform behavior.
buckets.doesNotProve: The Haxe preview lane is nonblocking, and TS7 generated-output success does not imply a TS7 programmatic API.

buckets.label: ESM/CommonJS/subpath/declaration-ingestion package shapes
buckets.scope: Manual externs and deterministic dts2hx-generated externs consumed through TS and classic Genes profiles.
buckets.proves: The named package and import forms resolve, type-check, and execute through the tested profiles without weak generated extern types. The focused identity fixture also keeps same-named default, named, and namespace exports distinct across TS, classic JS, and both declaration surfaces. Package-backed native String/RegExp constructors retain value-derived public instance types, while missing contracts fail before publication. Its hxnodejs-style extern enum abstract, same-named module-field imports, and typed Node process/console globals preserve exact runtime values and source ownership under the stable gate. The same command is enrolled in the advisory Haxe preview lane and rejects raw __js__ leakage.
buckets.doesNotProve: Four synthetic packages do not cover every package.json condition, declaration merge, built-in native name, abstract shape, module-field shape, bundler, or host environment. The Haxe preview lane remains advisory rather than a supported release contract.

buckets.label: Pinned PiMonoHX and OpenCodeHX pressure tests
buckets.scope: Pinned, network-isolated build/typecheck/local-smoke subsets from two WIP application ports.
buckets.proves: Exact downstream revisions run under the centralized stable Node lane; reviewed downstream-owned failures require exact command, exit-code, and TypeScript diagnostic evidence while independent later stages continue.
buckets.doesNotProve: A matched downstream-owned exception is not a compiler correctness proof; every unmatched failure remains unclassified until minimized, and a downstream pass is smoke evidence rather than semantic parity.

policy.network: OS-level network isolation after dependency bootstrap; loopback remains available for local fixture servers.
policy.failureOwnership: A reviewed downstream-owned failure is recognized only by its exact pinned command, exit code, and complete TypeScript diagnostic set. Every mismatch remains unclassified, and no failure becomes a compiler defect until reduced to a generic genes fixture.
policy.fullApplications: Full evolving WIP application suites remain nonblocking release/manual evidence.

unsupported.reason: The port remains WIP and does not claim complete upstream Pi behavior.
Live providers, OAuth, credentials, and external network effects are outside the no-network compiler contract.
The port remains WIP and does not claim complete upstream OpenCode behavior.
Live package-manager and external provider effects are outside the no-network compiler contract.
